remaining_proposals: Contact-force projection, phase-state bank, confidence joint-prior reweighting, PPO comparison and validated optional WM remain future controlled tests; they are not part of the current run.
objective: Improve unassisted Track 2 AUC, SP-SR, MP-SR and MPPE per total GPU-hour by extending the pinned native CHORD learner.

baseline.controller: frozen SONIC with all native body and finger residuals
baseline.reference_change: Our contact-aware retargeting inputs, before/after correction; not NVIDIA's upstream retargeting reproduction.
baseline.retired_from_primary_path: The paused custom PyTorch SAC plus per-episode full-state world-model learner. Preserve its artifacts.

keep: Native simulator, robot and object assets, actuator dynamics, SONIC and full-body residual interface
Native object tracking, balance, regularization and contact-wrench rewards as the controlled starting point
Corrected robot pose as a confidence-weighted soft prior, not dynamically feasible action supervision

dynamics_guidance.target: Smooth the permitted object trajectory, estimate uncertainty, and compute the required net wrench about the actual simulator COM using its mass and inertia.
dynamics_guidance.torque: I * angular_acceleration + angular_velocity cross (I * angular_velocity), in object coordinates
dynamics_guidance.support: Account for table/floor/other-object contact wrench before attributing the required remainder to the hands. Do not credit virtual assistance as robot contact force.
dynamics_guidance.feasibility: Project required hand wrench onto candidate contact-force sets with unilateral contact, friction and available force/torque bounds. Keep slack and uncertainty rather than certifying the trajectory.
dynamics_guidance.reward: Test a robust, dimensionless distance between required wrench and live achievable/realized wrench. Normalize torque by a characteristic length and force by a physical scale; confidence-weight unreliable accelerations and contact hypotheses.
dynamics_guidance.compute: Precompute reference derivatives and phase-level targets. First use cheap live support-function features already available in CHORD; profile before introducing per-step optimization.
dynamics_guidance.novelty_hypothesis: CHORD transfers demonstrated contact-wrench capability; this extension asks whether contacts can generate the wrench required by the object's task dynamics, even when the corrected joint path remains imperfect.

adaptive_curriculum.borrowed_from: DexMachina's reward/episode-length-gated reduction of virtual object control
adaptive_curriculum.extension: Use contact engagement, normalized wrench deficit and held-out lower-assistance probes to decide reductions, with a scheduled zero-assistance cohort and stall deadline.
adaptive_curriculum.training_resets: Use dynamically reached states from physical rollouts for phase starts, then progressively require longer prefixes and frame-zero starts. Do not assume corrected reference states are valid simulator states.
adaptive_curriculum.evaluation: Always full episode from the prescribed start, no virtual assistance or in-attempt resets.
adaptive_curriculum.anti_shortcut: High assisted tracking reward alone cannot advance the curriculum or select the winning checkpoint.

optimizer_ablation.candidate: Native PPO already present in the pinned CHORD runtime
optimizer_ablation.rationale: Test the optimizer separately using the same observations, actions, rewards, resets and assistance conditions; DexMachina's PPO results do not prove PPO is cheaper than FlashSAC here.
optimizer_ablation.schedule_alignment: Compare curriculum progress by physical transitions or measured competence, never equate PPO iteration count with SAC update count.
optimizer_ablation.decision: Choose by unassisted quality-versus-total-wall-time curves, not raw transitions/s. Keep FlashSAC if PPO does not win.

v2_optional_shared_world_model.architecture: Analytic integration and kinematics plus a compact learned residual for action-to-motion/contact response. Keep necessary body, finger, object, contact-mode and actuator/controller state; update known histories deterministically rather than predicting every stored scalar.
v2_optional_shared_world_model.sharing: Share across allowed episodes with compatible robot/controller physics and object-geometry/mass/inertia/friction conditioning. Reuse a common initialization for comparison arms and track data provenance; do not leak Tier 1 clean trajectories into Tier 2/3.
v2_optional_shared_world_model.pretrained_prior: The already acquired SuperMimic_Dyn checkpoint models 29-DoF G1 body tracking, not Dex3-object manipulation or our 43-action residual interface. Test a mapped body prior only if useful; it is not a ready manipulation WM.
validation: Held-out contiguous simulator windows split by rollout, emphasizing grasp, slip, release and falls
Short-rollout state/contact prediction compared with analytic and no-WM baselines
Action ranking and directional gradients checked by small real-simulator perturbations; low state MSE alone is insufficient
End-to-end quality at matched GPU time including model data collection and fitting
v2_optional_shared_world_model.policy_use_if_validated: Freeze model parameters during each short differentiable actor rollout, bootstrap with the real-data critic, restrict extrapolation, and replace a bounded amount of policy-update compute rather than simply stacking model training on top of all existing updates.
v2_optional_shared_world_model.initial_horizon_candidate: 4-8 steps for contact-rich manipulation; a hypothesis to validate, not SuperMimic's published H=32 configuration
v2_optional_shared_world_model.deployment: The submitted policy and SONIC do not require the training-only WM.

proposed_bounded_sequence: Recover baseline quality-versus-time curves from already saved native checkpoints; evaluation only, no baseline retraining.
On corrected Tier 1 episode 5, test adaptive curriculum alone against native FlashSAC, with fixed wall-time checkpoints and unassisted evaluation.
Add dynamics-targeted wrench guidance under the same learner and budget to isolate its effect.
Compare native PPO against FlashSAC only after fixing the environment/reward/curriculum contract.
Train the compact WM on allowed physical transitions in shadow mode, then run an otherwise matched WM-on/off test if prediction and gradient checks pass.
Promote a variant only after checking a second seed and episode, then Tier 2. Stop poor candidates at predeclared budgets; do not launch another blind four-by-350M queue.

reporting.claim_gate: Equal or better unassisted quality at lower total cost on matched inputs, with no hidden pretraining cost or omitted failed rollouts.
reporting.reference: Always name tier input versus clean evaluation reference, coverage, seed count and local AUC sample set.
